plotSections.title: Spirits outside town
bullets: Sylan’s working theory is that he picks spirits up by walking through town, as on the last visit to Carlkin’s. He means to stay outside town while Gerk finds the sheriff.

Proximity is enough: the spirits are finished once he is close, drawn into him like air into a flame. He ties this to people who will not move on when their allotment of life ends, usually the undead or spirits without bodies, and says you cannot cheat her in the end.
He is unsure whether the trigger is a touch, their time being up, or their having been truly bad. He remembers the proprietor of Shades and Trades as a ghost he has been near and has not taken.

He recalls six souls with descriptions but no names, and will describe them to the sheriff rather than dig through notes. He remembers a sheriff watching the town and no mayor; he jokes that the party might count as the mayor and that they are not that responsible.

plotSections.title: Carlkin’s lighthouse
bullets: Gerk heads into the city for the sheriff. The others fly to Carlkin’s lighthouse. Glimmen and Araden land in and beside the streets; Araden curls her wings and keeps her tail off the shingles, then lets Elrus down.

Dana knocks as the point person. After a crate, a chain, and metal on metal, Carlkin opens and checks that Sylan and Gerk are not with them. Dana confirms they are absent and that there are no portals or shenanigans.

Carlkin recognizes the second dragon as the copper Araden, not Glimmen. Dana explains that Walker has been training with an established dragon rider, and that this dragon is his mentor’s. Benji pushes past Dana; Araden perks up. Elrus and Benji embrace. Benji says Elrus looks old for his age and asks about longer meditation; Elrus has been training his new recruit and calls Walker over.

Dana says the party already met Benji in The Reach, including during the Sunder Chase, though Walker had not introduced them. Carlkin identifies Benji as a warforged. The DM notes Elrus and Araden had not previously interacted with Benji.

Carlkin and Benji date their friendship to around the start of the Sunder Chase and dispute who gave whom the idea. They describe another copper dragon who is still around and is now a hoard dragon for that race. Riding with Araden would now be treated as cheating and grounds for disqualification. Carlkin calls it a death race.

They recall the party winning the Sunder Chase with Carlkin’s guidance. Carlkin slaps Ord and credits him with dispelling another ship, a use of magic he has not seen in generations, against the usual cannons, faster sails, and burning ships. A dragon simply outflying a ship is the other counter. Ord says someone else would have thought of the dispel eventually.

plotSections.title: The white helm
bullets: Dana raises the helm Walker apprehended, which he is wearing. Carlkin still treats a lich phylactery as the likely reading. Walker says it is not one and that it is very mundane. Carlkin calls it ornamental and hobgoblin-inspired.

Walker hands it over. Carlkin’s belt pouch opens to about two feet across; he dunks the helm in and snaps it shut. He enchanted the bag of holding to detect soul magic of the kind acquainted with a phylactery and to burst into flames on contact. Nothing happens at first, and he says it can be returned in ten to fifteen minutes.

Dana asks about the little eagle. Walker rolls a 27 perception and sees the pouch’s bottom-right corner smolder. The bag does not flash into flame; Carlkin tears it off his belt and it smolders across its surface like slow-burning moss.

Carlkin says a phylactery would have been a full fire. This slow burn means trace soul magic on the item, and maybe further enchantments. He accuses Walker of having understated it. Ciri whispers that it looks like a phylactery. Carlkin says it is not a full phylactery and that it does not look like an ordinary helm.

Walker, who is fire resistant and has his golden glove, reaches into the burning bag. The damage is negligible after resistance. The interior is only large enough for the helm and a little extra. The bag’s bottom burns through, and the rest fractures like over-tapped crystal and blows away burning.

He is left with a slightly smoking white helm, cool to the touch, taken from the Emperor. Carlkin invites him inside to identify what he has been wearing. Walker stays. Dana goes in out of curiosity, and Ciri follows to needle Walker.

chronologicalEvents: Sylan tells Gerk he likely picked up spirits by walking through town on the way to Carlkin’s, and that being close is enough for them to be drawn into him like air into a flame.
Sylan decides to stay outside town, recalls six souls by description rather than name, and asks Gerk to find the sheriff. He remembers no mayor.
Gerk leaves to look for the sheriff. The others fly to Carlkin’s lighthouse, where Glimmen and Araden land and Araden sets Elrus down.
Dana knocks. Carlkin confirms Sylan and Gerk are not with the party, then recognizes Araden as a copper dragon distinct from Glimmen.
Benji greets Araden and Elrus. Dana introduces herself and recalls meeting Benji in The Reach during the Sunder Chase. Carlkin identifies Benji as a warforged.

Carlkin and Benji connect their history to the early Sunder Chase, including another copper who is now a hoard dragon for the race, and Carlkin credits Ord with dispelling a ship when the party won it.
Walker removes the hobgoblin-inspired helm and Carlkin seals it in an enchanted bag of holding meant to burn on contact with phylactery soul magic.
Walker’s 27 perception catches the bag smoldering. Carlkin reads the slow burn as trace soul magic and possible further enchantments, not a full phylactery.
Walker pulls the white helm out with his golden glove. The bag burns apart. Carlkin takes Walker inside to study the helm further; Dana and Ciri go with them.

Sylan.existing: Half-elf rogue and Gilbrick Gatekeeper who holds a keystone and a cautious bond with the Raven Queen.
notes: He believes walking through town is how spirits reach him, based on the last trip to Carlkin’s.
Once he is close, they are drawn in like air into a flame. He describes the targets as people who refuse to move on at the end of their allotment, typically undead or spirits without bodies.
He has not taken the proprietor of Shades and Trades, whom he now remembers as a ghost after previously remembering a human.
He is staying outside town and can describe six souls but does not have their names.
He remembers this town as watched by a sheriff, with no mayor he ever met.
personality: He frames the work as finding those who will not accept that their time is over, and says you cannot cheat her in the end.
quotesThemes: You cannot cheat her in the end.
openQuestions: He is unsure whether a spirit is taken by touch, because its time is up, or because it was truly bad.

notes: He goes into the city to find the sheriff while Sylan stays outside town.
He is uneasy about identifying harmful spirits if Sylan is not in town, and about how anyone arrests something that is simply drawn into Sylan.

Carlkin.existing: Turtle-like proprietor of the New Navel lighthouse and bookshop.
notes: He answers only after a crate slides, a chain rattles, and metal rasps, and he checks that Sylan and Gerk were not brought.
He recognizes Araden on sight and is old friends with Benji, going back to around the start of the Sunder Chase.
He claims a hand in guiding the party’s Sunder Chase win and credits Ord with dispelling another ship.

He enchanted a bag of holding as a soul-cleaning apparatus: it detects soul magic associated with a phylactery and should burst into flames on contact. The helm only made it smolder, which he reads as trace soul magic plus possible other enchantments.
The bag burned away like fracturing crystal. He invites Walker inside to identify the helm.
personality: Wary of Sylan and Gerk’s portals and shenanigans, and fond of the Sunder Chase, which he calls a fun death race.

Benji.existing: Someone familiar with The Reach whom the party met there.
notes: He is a warforged. The party already heard that explanation in The Reach, and he was with them when they completed the Sunder Chase.
He is at Carlkin’s lighthouse, greets Araden, and cordially embraces Elrus. Carlkin says the party, Araden, and Elrus had not previously interacted with him together.
He and Carlkin go back to about when the Sunder Chase began, and they dispute which of them supplied the idea.
He remarks that Elrus looks old for his age and asks if he has been meditating longer.

Araden.existing: A magically capable companion brought secretly to The Reach.
notes: She is a copper dragon. Dana identifies her as the dragon of the established dragon rider mentoring Walker, not as Glimmen.
She lands beside the lighthouse, tucks her wings, and keeps her tail from tearing off shingles, then lets Elrus down.
She visibly perks up when Benji comes toward her. Carlkin knows her from long ago.
Carlkin says entering the Sunder Chase with Araden would now be considered cheating and would get a rider disqualified.
Araden carries him to Carlkin’s door and lets him down.
He cordially embraces Benji, says he has been training his new recruit, and calls Walker over to meet Benji.

Walker.existing: Half-elf dragon rider and fighter bonded to Glimmen.
notes: He has been training with an established dragon rider; Araden is that mentor’s dragon.
He was wearing the white helm and does not believe it is a phylactery. He calls it very mundane.
A 27 perception check lets him see Carlkin’s pouch start to smolder.
He is fire resistant and carries a golden glove. He reaches into the burning bag and recovers the helm with negligible damage.
He agrees to stay in the lighthouse while Carlkin studies the helm.

Ord.existing: Dragonborn paladin and Gatekeeper of Feldspar.
notes: Carlkin credits him with the clever move in the party’s Sunder Chase win: dispelling another ship, something Carlkin has not seen in generations.
Ord says someone else would have thought of it eventually.

Dana.existing: Half-elf cleric, most knowledgeable of the group.
notes: She takes the door as the designated point person, assures Carlkin that Sylan and Gerk are absent, and introduces herself to Benji.
She presses the phylactery question and then asks about the little eagle before the bag is seen to burn.
She goes into the lighthouse with Walker and Carlkin.

Helm.existing: A helm Carlkin agreed to examine.
notes: Walker had been wearing it. It is a white helm he took from the Emperor, ornamental and hobgoblin-inspired.
Carlkin’s soul-magic bag did not fully ignite. Carlkin concludes it is not a phylactery, but that trace soul magic accompanies it and that other enchantments may be present.
It is cool to the touch after being pulled from the smoldering bag. Carlkin is taking it inside for a closer identification.
openQuestions: What the helm actually is, beyond trace soul magic and possible further enchantments.

Sunder Chase.existing: A summer seasonal event in The Reach.
notes: Carlkin calls it a death race. Usual entries rely on cannons, faster sails, or burning ships. A dragon simply flying faster than a ship is the other route, and racing with Araden would now be cheating.
The party won it. Carlkin says he gave them guidance. Ord’s contribution was dispelling another ship.
Carlkin and Benji trace their friendship, and the argument over who had the idea, to when the Chase first started.
Another copper dragon is described as still around and now a hoard dragon for the race.

Shades and Trades.existing: Where Sylan found the staff later fused to Ord’s lantern.
notes: Sylan now believes its proprietor was a ghost. He remembers earlier thinking the proprietor was human, has been around him, and has not taken him.

New Navel.existing: A familiar stop that holds Carlkin’s lighthouse and sends trade to the party’s tavern.
notes: Sylan remembers a sheriff as the person who watched the town, and no mayor. He suggests the party might jokingly occupy that role.
Dragons landing near the lighthouse draw a stir in the streets.
Carlkin says the white helm Walker has been wearing is the one Walker took from the Emperor.

misTranscriptions.notes: Gerk asks how you arrest one as it is sucked into Sylan.
Gerk, overlapping Sylan’s air-into-a-flame line. No stable phrase is clear.
Sylan on the proprietor he now thinks was a ghost.
Carlkin checking who was brought to the door.
Carlkin asking whether the copper dragon is Walker’s own dragon.
Carlkin greeting the copper dragon. Also heard nearby as Rayadin.
Benji telling Elrus he looks old for his age.
Said of the other copper who is now a hoard dragon for the race. Benji and Carlkin are both talking.
Carlkin shifting into how the party won it.
What brings you back to Carlkin so soon.
Carlkin dismissing magic, contrasted with cannons, faster sails, and burning ships. Ord’s dispel is the intended example.
Dana asks what Carlkin was saying about it immediately before the pouch is seen smoldering. Nothing in the chunk identifies it.
Carlkin on the helm after it comes out of the bag.

openQuestions: Sylan does not know whether spirits are taken because of a touch, because their time is up, or because they were truly bad.
Dana asks about the little eagle and the chunk never answers it.
Carlkin has not yet said what the white helm is. The bag test rules out a full phylactery and shows trace soul magic, with possible further enchantments.

newTerms.name: Walker's golden glove
notes: Walker uses it, with his fire resistance, to pull the helm from Carlkin’s burning bag.

newTerms.name: Carlkin's soul-cleaning bag
notes: A bag of holding he enchanted to detect phylactery soul magic and ignite on contact. The helm only made it smolder, and the bag then burned away.

newTerms.name: The Emperor
notes: Carlkin says Walker took the white helm from the Emperor.
